title: Coffee-clutch passback: Joel Bates - runtime candidate
content:
Quick scribble after a 30m informal convo over coffee with candidate (senior runtime). Informal notes, rough impressions, follow-ups.

Context:
- Role: Senior Inference Engineer (serving runtime)
- Format: 30m informal chat + 20m pairing slot scheduled later
- Came from infra-heavy startup, built internal serving for seq2seq models

TL;DR: Smart engineer, practical bias, good latency intuition. Not deep on quant kernels or CUDA micro-optimizations but strong at system-level tradeoffs and product-facing constraints. Comfortable owning a rolling deploy pipeline and incident ops.

Strengths:
- Clear mental model for async batching + backpressure; sketched an autoscaling heuristic that combined queue depth + p50 latency trends. Simple and effective.
- Good runbook instincts: wants explicit SLO->playbook mapping and can write postmortems that surface remediation steps + metrics.
- Product-sensitivity: asked about cost-per-token and suggested a feature to expose per-route cache-hit metrics to product teams.

Weaknesses / Unknowns:
- Limited exposure to custom CUDA kernels and low-level operator fusion; hasn't shipped quantized kernels in prod, mostly used vendor libs and XLA-like toolchains.
- KV cache strategy: comfortable with high-level cache invalidation but unclear on multi-tenant memory fragmentation strategies for long-lived sessions. Needs follow-up design problem.
- Scale pedigree: good at ~hundreds of qps sustained, less clear about 1k+ simultaneous streaming sessions on multi-GPU sharded KV cache.

Pairing impressions (mini pairing scheduled):
- Good communicator during thought process, asks clarifying questions, proposes incremental deliverables rather than big-bang redesigns.
- Tends to prefer pragmatic workarounds (sharded LRU segments) over theoretical optimality — aligns with what we want for shipping.

Red flags (not blocking):
- Has one public repo with experimental kernels but it's unmaintained for 18 months. Might need ramp on maintenance standards.
- Slight tendency to default to language-level concurrency models (Go goroutines) — our stack is mostly C++ + Python + CUDA; check familiarity.

Calibration notes for hiring committee:
- Score: 6.5/10 — strong SRE/ops + systems thinking, medium infra-optimal low-level engineering.
- Role fit: Good for runtime reliability, rollout/ops; needs pairing with applied-ml or kernel engineer for quant/kernel work.

Open questions / follow-ups before next loop:
1) Ask candidate to whiteboard a multi-GPU KV cache eviction strategy for mixed short/long sessions (we should give them 45m to sketch with diagrams).
2) Short take-home: small microbenchmark harness — implement a prefix caching shim that returns cached tokens for repeated prefixes and measure latency under bursty load (we'll give 48h).
3) Confirm comfort level with C++ code review and diagnosing GPU OOMs in production (ask for a past incident story).

Action items (my suggested next steps):
- Invite to pairing session (1h) focused on design + code review (schedule next week).
- Send take-home spec (lightweight) if pairing goes well.
- Prep two calibration questions for panel about: memory fragmentation for long-lived KV caches, and rolling deploy fallback policies when model variants diverge on latency.

Links and refs I mentioned during chat:
- Confluence: infra/serving/kv-cache-design (asked candidate if they'd seen our draft notes)
- Jira: SERVE-4219 (we should attach take-home as linked ticket)
- GH PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/342 (candidate asked about our runtime testing infra)

Notes-to-self / random musings:
- Candidate liked idea to surface route-level cache hit heatmaps in console — maybe prod-ops asks want this.
- If we hire: pair first 2 months with kernel engineer (mentor) + run a mini-project on cache eviction policies.
- Keep this doc short and share with hiring buddy before loop.

Raw snippets from convo (verbatim-ish):
- "I usually prefer to bias toward correctness first, then optimize hot paths once we have measurements."
- "We had a crazy outlier once where a single session pinned a lot of GPU memory because of a long context — we implemented a soft-eviction that trimmed older KV shards and reduced incidents."

Recommendation: move to structured loop (pairing + take-home). Not yet a final hire/no-hire decision.

TODOs for me:

- Invite kernel pair (Mira Lin) to observe pairing session.
- Add 3 calibration questions to panel doc.
recommended_next_steps: Invite to 1h pairing focused on KV-cache design; issue lightweight take-home; pair with kernel mentor if loop goes well.
